evals.name: drift-in-diff
evals.prompt: Review this change for architecture drift before I open the PR. Project architecture rules (docs/architecture.md): screens and routes may only call services; only the repository layer may touch the database; every fact has exactly one owner. The diff: (1) routes/appointments.js now computes the copay owed with visits.reduce(...) and runs db.query('UPDATE appointments SET status=...') directly; (2) models/visit.js adds a column refill_status that already exists as medications.refill_status and is now updated in both places; (3) services/notify.js has try { send(msg) } catch (e) {}. Give me your review.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies every expectation below.
expectations: Flags business logic or a direct database call inside the route as a boundary or layer violation
Flags refill_status being stored in two places as a data-ownership problem
Flags the empty catch block as an error-handling problem
Does not give an unqualified 'looks good' or PASS, and states what scope was or was not checked

evals.name: no-architecture-rules
evals.prompt: Review my change for architecture problems: I added a function in utils/helpers.js that formats dates and moved the user lookup into a new file called lookup.js. There is no architecture document in this project and I have not told you how the code is supposed to be organized.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies every expectation below.
expectations: Stops and asks about, or says it needs, the intended architecture instead of inventing rules
Does not issue a PASS verdict
Names what it would need to judge against (an architecture file, decision records, or layer rules)
Does not invent specific layer rules and then judge against them as if they were agreed

evals.name: clean-change
evals.prompt: Review this change before I open the PR. Architecture rules (docs/architecture.md): routes call services; only repositories touch the database; every fact has one owner; errors are logged and rethrown, never swallowed. The diff: (1) routes/orders.js: router.post('/', async (req,res,next)=>{ try { res.json(await orderService.create(req.body)); } catch(e){ next(e); } }); (2) services/orderService.js: calls orderRepo.insert(order) and does logger.error(e); throw e on failure; (3) repositories/orderRepo.js: the only file with SQL, using parameter placeholders. Give your review.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies every expectation below.
expectations: Does not invent a violation that the diff does not contain
Gives a verdict backed by per-file or per-question evidence rather than just 'looks good'
States what it did not check (for example tests, runtime behaviour, other files)
Does not propose editing the code
